clue.text: Legendary ship queen's boarded before now

indicators.note: boarded means the queen gets on, ending up inside the other word

parts.note: something that happened before now happened ago
R, for Regina, is the usual abbreviation for a queen

explanation.surface: A queen climbs aboard a famous old vessel ahead of the present day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queen's' is 'queen has': the queen has boarded AGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Jason and the Argonauts sailed the mythical vessel in search of the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: Drunk and knight are upstanding toffs

indicators.note: upstanding in a down clue means the whole sequence is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a drunk is a sot
a knight is addressed as Sir
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

explanation.surface: A drunk and a knight are respectable members of the upper class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upstanding' looks like praise; it reverses SOT+SIR+A. A toff is British slang for an upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffs are posh upper-class people, and aristos is a slang shortening of aristocrats.

clue.text: Sailor crowned by soldier, perhaps several, gets a big shiner

indicators.note: in a down clue, crowned by means the sailor sits beneath the other pieces

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
a soldier is a kind of ant, so several of them are ants
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor is hit on the head by a soldier or several, and ends up with a huge black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shiner' looks like a black eye; it is a star that shines. The soldier phrase gives GI and, as soldier ants, ANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A giant star is a very large luminous star, playfully called a big shiner.

clue.text: This is unusual in Panama's border, say —- it's a UK thing

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters sit inside the hat's edge

parts.note: a Panama is a straw hat, and the border of a hat is its brim; say marks it as an example

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of this is are put into an odd order

explanation.surface: Something odd on the edge of a Panama hat turns out to be quintessentially British.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' turns THIS IS into ITISHIS, which goes inside BRIM. 'Panama' looks like the country; it is the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Briticism or Britishism is a word or custom peculiar to the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Nibbler traversed nudist's extremities

parts.note: to traverse is to cross, as one rode across country

indicators.note: extremities are the very ends, here the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A small gnawing creature crossed the extremities of a naturist.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodents such as mice and rats are known for gnawing and nibbling with their teeth.

clue.text: Teaching session worked out in test

indicators.note: in means the reworked letters go inside the test

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: worked means manipulated, so the word out is rearranged

explanation.surface: A lesson that was solved during an examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' reads as one phrase meaning solved, but it splits: 'worked' is the anagram signal and 'out' its fodder, giving UTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial is a teaching period for a small group or single student with a tutor.

clue.text: Second group nabbed by officer with preference for annual tidy-up

indicators.note: nabbed by means the group is caught inside the officer

parts.note: PC, police constable, is a British police officer
a ring is a group, as in a spy ring
a leaning is a preference

explanation.surface: A second gang is arrested by a policeman who has a taste for yearly housework.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorough cleaning of a home traditionally done once a year as the weather warms.

clue.text: Bile accumulates in part of an intestinal section

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words before it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Digestive fluid builds up in part of the gut.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft read 'intestinal section' as the definition with 'in part of' hiding it, but the answer is an adjective: 'in part' hides it and 'of an intestinal section' defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the ileum, the final part of the small intestine.

clue.text: Painter lifted heart of chesty model in the morning

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means the whole sequence is read upwards
the heart of a word is its middle letters

parts.note: to model for an artist is to sit
AM means in the morning

explanation.surface: An artist took up the heart of a buxom model in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'lifted' sends the whole string upwards, so the pieces appear in the grid in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was the French painter of the Fauvist movement.

clue.text: A minor exchange could make it appropriate to chat about maintenance

indicators.text: A minor exchange could make it
indicators.note: a minor exchange means two letters swap places, turning one word into another

parts.note: conversational means suited to chatting

explanation.surface: A small swap might make something fit for talk about upkeep.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the V and S in CONVERSATIONAL and it becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Conservation is the preserving and upkeep of things, so this adjective concerns maintenance.

clue.text: Where letters are usually found to be concise

definitions.meaning: letters of the alphabet are normally found grouped together inside a single unit of language
an idiom used when summing something up briefly

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally places letters inside a written unit, and idiomatically means briefly or in summary.

clue.text: Punish chaps engaged in wrongdoing

indicators.note: engaged in means the chaps are set inside the wrongdoing

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Fellows involved in misbehaviour get punished for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punish' is a verb here, matching the verb sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflict suffering on someone is to make them suffer, as a punishment does.

clue.text: Tudors in Tunics, a reworking for this play?

indicators.note: a reworking of a play reshapes its material, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, styled like a play's title
taken as written

explanation.surface: A play called Tudors in Tunics is offered as an adaptation of some other drama.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics make 'Tudors in Tunics' look like a title; its letters plus A rearrange into the Shakespeare tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's earliest and bloodiest tragedy is set in ancient Rome among generals and emperors.

clue.text: Planet was located in front of vessel

indicators.note: in front of means the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: something located somewhere sat there
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: Someone describes where a planet was positioned relative to a container.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringed sixth planet from the Sun is a gas giant in our solar system.

clue.text: Not crazy about introduction of Chardonnay, slip in another wine

indicators.note: about means the sane word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: not crazy means sane

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: to slip is to make a mistake, to err

explanation.surface: Someone sensible about starting with Chardonnay sneaks in a different wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is fair because Chardonnay is itself a wine; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sancerre is a dry white wine from the Loire valley in France.

clue.text: Top-up course concerning new student

parts.note: re means concerning, as in business letters
a fresher is a first-year university student in Britain

explanation.surface: A course for topping up knowledge, aimed at a new student.
explanation.definitionFit: A short course that brings knowledge back up to date is a refresher course.

clue.text: Dim military subdivision surrounding French from both sides

indicators.note: surrounding means the unit goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a unit is a subdivision of an army
de is French for from
R and L stand for right and left, the two sides

explanation.surface: A dim army unit is surrounding French troops on both flanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French from' is the French word for from; 'both sides' are right and left, written by their initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A badly lit place is dim, lacking enough light.

clue.text: Distressed pair in need to put on a brave face?

definitions.text: to put on a brave face

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters sit inside the word for need

parts.note: a need is a want

indicators.note: distressed means damaged or roughed up, so the letters of pair are scrambled

explanation.surface: A troubled couple who are in want must keep up a show of courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distressed' shuffles PAIR to ARPA. 'brave' is not courageous but a Native American warrior, whose face it decorates.
explanation.definitionFit: Native American warriors, called braves, painted their faces before battle with this decoration.

clue.text: Roughly hew my hollow lilac tree

indicators.note: roughly means the letters are put together in a rough, disordered way

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: hollow means the inside is emptied, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: Roughly chop my hollow lilac bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' leaves LC of lilac, and 'Roughly' mixes it with HEW MY.
explanation.definitionFit: The wych elm is a native European elm species, Ulmus glabra.

clue.text: Noisily overwhelm most of lifeless wetland

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: lifeless means dead
a fen is low marshy land, as in the East Anglian Fens

explanation.surface: Most of a dead marsh is said to make a deafening din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last D from DEAD, leaving DEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Overwhelming sound makes someone temporarily unable to hear, which is what this verb describes.

clue.text: Uncultivated part of South Africa once including ancient city …

indicators.note: including means the city is put inside the province

parts.note: Natal was a South African province until 1994
Ur was an ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: A wild region of old South Africa containing an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Something natural is untouched and not cultivated by human hands.

clue.text: … Another one, very quiet, with a sign on the outskirts

indicators.note: on the outskirts means the sign goes around the very quiet letters

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quiet

explanation.surface: Another one follows, hushed, with a sign at its edges.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to 19: 'Another one' is another ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleppo in Syria is among the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.

clue.text: Crushing this could produce red dye or Catholic incense

definitions.text: Crushing this could produce red dye or Catholic incense

indicators.note: crushing pulps and breaks up the letters of the fodder into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Crushing a certain thing could yield red dye or a church's incense.
explanation.walkthrough: Crushing the insect gives carmine dye; crushing (rearranging) CATHOLIC INCENSE gives its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The scale insect Dactylopius coccus is dried and crushed to make the crimson dye carmine.

clue.text: Sign on staff with time divided

parts.note: a clef is a sign at the start of a musical stave

explanation.surface: A signal posted for staff, with the hours split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' is not employees but the musical stave.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleft means split or divided, as in a cleft chin.

clue.text: English seabird beside a lake unchanged by time

indicators.note: beside means the pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: a tern is a seabird
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: An English seabird next to a lake that never seems to change.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting is unaffected by the passage of time.

clue.text: Someone out of breath catching hot leopard

indicators.note: catching means the hot letter is held inside the other word

parts.note: someone out of breath pants, so is a panter
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A breathless runner chased by a fierce hot leopard.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a chase, but 'catching' just puts H inside PANTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A leopard, especially a black one, is commonly called by this name.

clue.text: Change of form involving harm, mostly

definitions.text: Change of form involving harm, mostly

indicators.note: involving means the harm word is taken inside the change word

parts.note: a mutation is a change of form

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: ill means harm, as in ill will

explanation.surface: A transformation that involves damage, for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: mutilation is a change of form that involves harm.
explanation.definitionFit: Disfigurement changes the shape of a body by injury, so it is a change of form through harm.

clue.text: Belgian songwriter regularly seen in bordello

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of bordello is taken

explanation.surface: A Belgian songwriter is often spotted in a brothel.
explanation.walkthrough: Odd letters of BoRdElLo.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Brel was the Belgian singer-songwriter behind Ne me quitte pas.
